name: binary/values-and-dictionary
about: RB's tag bytes and its key dictionary. The dictionary is the part with history: spec 09 listed 38 protocol keys while both codecs held 40, so every schema-derived id was two out from what the document described. Nothing failed, because each runtime only ever spoke to itself. A third implementation built from the text would have disagreed with both about the meaning of every key, and had nothing to check itself against - which is what these vectors are for.
source: spec 09 §2 for the tags and §3 for the dictionary. Every byte string below was written out by hand from those tables - the tag, then the payload - rather than captured from a codec.
rule: One tag byte, then payload. Integers 0-127 are the single byte 0x80|n; anything else is 0x03 and a zigzag varint.
A double is 0x04 and eight little-endian IEEE 754 bytes, used only when the value is not an integer.
A string is 0x05, a varint length, UTF-8; it joins the per-frame string table. 0x06 and a varint index refers back to one.
A list is 0x07 and a varint count, then values. An object is 0x08 and a varint count, then key/value pairs.
An object key is a varint k: even k is the dictionary id k/2, odd k is an inline UTF-8 key of length (k-1)/2.
Ids 0-39 are the protocol keys, in the order given below; schema names follow, sorted.

values.name: the largest inline integer
values.why: 0x80 | 127, the last value the one-byte form reaches

values.name: one past it needs the tagged form
values.why: zigzag(128) = 256, and 256 as a varint is 0x80 0x02

values.name: a non-integer is a double, little-endian
a repeated string is a reference into the frame's table
values.why: list of 2, the string at index 0, then 0x06 and that index

values.name: a protocol key is a dictionary id
values.why: id is dictionary 0, so the key varint is 0; the value 1 is inline

values.name: the second-to-last protocol key
values.why: list is dictionary 38, so k = 76 = 0x4c. A codec whose dictionary stops at 38 keys has no id for this and writes it inline instead

values.name: the last protocol key
values.why: ins is dictionary 39, so k = 78 = 0x4e. These two are the keys spec 09 omitted, and they are why the count is load-bearing

values.name: a key the dictionary does not have is inline
values.why: k = 2*2+1 = 5 for a two-byte key, then its UTF-8
